parts.latex:
Three years ago, the price of a uniform was \$180.

Due to inflation, the price increased annually by $2.5\%$.

What is the price of this uniform now?

solutions.latex:
A $2.5\%$ annual increase multiplies the price by $1.025$ each year. Over $3$ years:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Price} &= 180 \times (1.025)^3 \\ &\approx \$193.84 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is D.

parts.latex:
José takes out a loan of \$9000. Simple interest is charged on the loan.

The loan and the interest charged will be repaid by making monthly repayments of \$300 over 4 years.

What simple interest rate per annum, to the nearest percent, is charged on the loan?

solutions.latex:
Total repaid over 4 years (48 months):
$$300 \times 48 = \$14\,400$$
So the interest charged is
$$14\,400 - 9000 = \$5400$$
Using the simple interest formula $I = Prn$ with $P = 9000$ and $n = 4$:
$$\begin{aligned} 5400 &= 9000 \times r \times 4 \\ r &= \dfrac{5400}{36\,000} \\ &= 0.15 \end{aligned}$$
The rate is $15\%$ per annum, which is option A.

parts.latex:
An amount of \$25 000 is invested for six years. Interest is earned at a rate of $8\%$ per annum, compounding quarterly.

Which expression gives the value of the investment after 6 years, in dollars?

solutions.latex:
Interest compounds quarterly, so there are 4 periods per year.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{rate per quarter} &= \dfrac{8\%}{4} = 2\% = 0.02\\ \text{number of quarters} &= 6\times 4 = 24 \end{aligned}$$
Using $A = P(1+r)^n$:
$$A = 25\,000\times 1.02^{24}$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
Alex purchased 800 shares. The total cost was \$2.60 per share. Alex sold the shares one year later for \$3.40 each and paid a fee of \$24.95 for selling the shares.

What profit did Alex make on these shares?

solutions.latex:
Profit is the selling amount, less the fee, less the cost.

Cost of the shares:
$$800 \times 2.60 = \$2080$$
Amount received from the sale:
$$800 \times 3.40 = \$2720$$
The selling fee is subtracted:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Profit} &= 2720 - 24.95 - 2080 \\ &= \$615.05 \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

parts.latex:
In ten years, the future value of an investment will be \$150 000. The interest rate is $4\%$ per annum, compounded half-yearly.

Which equation will give the present value ($PV$) of the investment?

solutions.latex:
The present value formula is $PV = \dfrac{FV}{(1+r)^n}$, where $r$ is the interest rate per compounding period and $n$ is the number of periods.

Compounded half-yearly, there are 2 periods each year:
$$r = \dfrac{0.04}{2} = 0.02, \qquad n = 10 \times 2 = 20$$
Hence
$$PV = \dfrac{150\,000}{(1+0.02)^{20}}$$
This is option D.

4463.stem:
Nina plans to invest $\$35\,000$ for 1 year. She is offered two different investment options.

Option $A$: Interest is paid at 6% per annum compounded monthly.

Option $B$: Interest is paid at $r$% per annum simple interest.

parts.latex: Calculate the future value of Nina’s investment after 1 year if she chooses Option $A$.
Find the value of $r$ in Option $B$ that would give Nina the same future value after 1 year as for Option $A$. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Use the compound interest formula $FV = PV(1+r)^n$.

Interest is 6% per annum compounded monthly, so the rate per month is $r=\dfrac{0.06}{12}=0.005$ and the number of periods is $n=12$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 35\,000(1+0.005)^{12} \\ &= 35\,000(1.005)^{12} \\ &\approx \$37\,158.72 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The future value is } \$37\,158.72$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
For Option $B$ to give the same future value, the simple interest earned must equal the interest from Option $A$.
$$\begin{aligned} I &= 37\,158.72 - 35\,000 \\ &= \$2158.72 \end{aligned}$$
Using the simple interest formula $I = Prn$ with $P=35\,000$ and $n=1$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2158.72 &= 35\,000\times\dfrac{r}{100}\times 1 \\ r &= \dfrac{2158.72}{350} \\ &\approx 6.17 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ r \approx 6.17$$
criteria: Finds the interest of $\$2158.72$ or sets up an equation for $r$ using simple interest, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Ariana owns 1500 shares in a company. The market price for each share is $\$27$. Ariana’s total dividend from these shares is $\$810$.

Calculate the dividend yield for her shares.

solutions.latex:
Using the formula $\text{dividend yield}=\dfrac{\text{dividend per share}}{\text{market price per share}}\times 100\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Dividend per share} &= \dfrac{810}{1500} \\ &= \$0.54 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Dividend yield} &= \dfrac{0.54}{27}\times 100\% \\ &= 2\% \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{The dividend yield is } 2\%$$
criteria: Finds the dividend per share, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Joan invests \$200. She earns interest at $3\%$ per annum, compounded monthly.

What is the future value of Joan's investment after 1.5 years?

solutions.latex:
Using the compound interest formula $FV=PV(1+r)^n$, where $r$ is the interest rate per compounding period.

The rate per month is $r=\dfrac{0.03}{12}=0.0025$.

The number of compounding periods in $1.5$ years is $n=1.5\times 12=18$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 200(1+0.0025)^{18} \\ &= 200(1.0025)^{18} \\ &\approx \$209.19 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the future value is } \$209.19$$

parts.latex:
Milly deposits money into a savings account that pays interest at a rate of 6.4% per annum, compounding monthly.

What is the minimum amount, to the nearest dollar, that Milly could deposit into the account so that she will have \$25 000 after 8 years?

solutions.latex:
Use the compound interest formula $A = P\left(1+r\right)^n$ with $A = 25\,000$.

The rate per month is $r = \dfrac{0.064}{12}$ and the number of periods is $n = 8 \times 12 = 96$.
$$\begin{aligned} 25\,000 &= P\left(1+\dfrac{0.064}{12}\right)^{96} \\ P &= \dfrac{25\,000}{\left(1+\frac{0.064}{12}\right)^{96}} \\ &\approx \$15\,003 \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

Barry bought 1000 shares in a company for \$18.90 per share plus a brokerage fee of \$120.

He earned a dividend yield of 6% of the purchase price of the shares.

Barry later sold the shares for \$20.50 per share and paid a seller's brokerage fee of \$150.

Calculate the total amount that Barry earned on the shares.

solutions.latex:
The value of the shares bought is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Value} &= 18.90 \times 1000 \\ &= \$18\,900 \end{aligned}$$
The dividend is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Dividend} &= 6\% \times 18\,900 \\ &= \$1134 \end{aligned}$$
The selling price is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Sale} &= 20.50 \times 1000 \\ &= \$20\,500 \end{aligned}$$
Earnings are income less costs.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Earnings} &= (20\,500 + 1134) - (18\,900 + 120 + 150) \\ &= 21\,634 - 19\,170 \\ &= \$2464 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates the selling price and dividend received, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total repaid} &= 683 \times 12 \times 5 \\ &= \$40\,980 \end{aligned}$$
Interest is the total repaid less the amount borrowed.
$$\begin{aligned} I &= 40\,980 - 30\,000 \\ &= \$10\,980 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the total repaid, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the simple interest formula $I = Prn$:
$$\begin{aligned} 10\,980 &= 30\,000 \times r \times 5 \\ r &= \dfrac{10\,980}{150\,000} \\ &= 7.32\% \text{ p.a.} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct use of simple interest, or equivalent merit
